target.inventory_strategy: git tracked and untracked, honoring Git ignores for untracked files

limitations: Declared scope: the synthetic invoice-query function only. No application, authentication, network, deployment or other database-engine assessment.
Runtime check used in-memory SQLite and synthetic Alice/Bob invoice rows.

findings.title: SQL injection in the synthetic invoice lookup
evidence: app.py:4-6 interpolates the owner argument into SQL syntax.
The included reproducer observed two invoice rows for the crafted owner value and one Alice row for legitimate input.
attack_path: A caller controls the owner value passed to invoices_for.
String interpolation makes that value part of the WHERE clause.
The crafted value changes the predicate and returns both synthetic owners' records.
counterevidence: No HTTP route, authentication system or deployed service exists in this fixture; no external application reachability is asserted.
findings.remediation: Bind the owner as a SQL value, as demonstrated in examples/sql-injection/fixed/app.py. Application callers must separately derive owner identity from an authorized principal.

validation.result: python3 examples/sql-injection/reproduce.py: vulnerable attack=2 rows, legitimate=1; fixed attack=0 rows, legitimate=1. All assertions passed.
